101.solution:
Build the truth table for \(\lbrack p ightarrow (q \land \sim p)brack \vee \lbrack (p \vee \sim q) \land pbrack\).

For rows \((p,q)\):
- \((T,T)\): \(q \land \sim p = T \land F = F\); \(p ightarrow F = F\). \((p \vee \sim q) \land p = (T \vee F) \land T = T\). Disjunction \(= F \vee T = T\).
- \((T,F)\): \(q \land \sim p = F\); \(p ightarrow F = F\). \((p \vee \sim q) \land p = (T \vee T) \land T = T\). \(F \vee T = T\).
- \((F,T)\): \(q \land \sim p = T \land T = T\); \(p ightarrow T = T\). \((p \vee \sim q) \land p = (F \vee F) \land F = F\). \(T \vee F = T\).
- \((F,F)\): \(q \land \sim p = F\); \(p ightarrow F = T\) (since \(p\) is false). \((p \vee \sim q) \land p = (\ldots) \land F = F\). \(T \vee F = T\).

The last column is \(T\,T\,T\,T\).

102.subtopic: Section Formula, Concurrency, Foot of Perpendicular, and Distance
102.solution:
The two given lines are \(l_1: 4x + 3y = 10\) and \(l_2: 8x + 6y + 5 = 0\), i.e. \(4x + 3y = -	frac{5}{2}\). Both have slope \(-	frac{4}{3}\), so they are parallel; a line through \(O\) crosses them at \(A\) and \(B\), and \(O\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio of the perpendicular distances from \(O\) to each line.

Distance from \(O\) to \(l_1\): \(d_1 = \dfrac{|{-10}|}{\sqrt{4^2+3^2}} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\).

Distance from \(O\) to \(l_2\) (\(8x+6y+5=0\)): \(d_2 = \dfrac{|5|}{\sqrt{8^2+6^2}} = \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

Hence \(AO:OB = d_1:d_2 = 2:	frac{1}{2} = 4:1\).

103.subtopic: Rate of Change and Related Rates
103.solution:
The position is \(x = a + bt - ct^2,\; y = at + bt^2\). The acceleration components are the second derivatives.

\(\dfrac{dx}{dt} = b - 2ct \Rightarrow \dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -2c\).

\(\dfrac{dy}{dt} = a + 2bt \Rightarrow \dfrac{d^2y}{dt^2} = 2b\).

Resultant acceleration \(= \sqrt{(-2c)^2 + (2b)^2} = \sqrt{4c^2 + 4b^2} = 2\sqrt{b^2 + c^2}\) unit/second\(^2\).

104.subtopic: Vector Geometry — Section Formula, Triangle, and Parallelogram
104.solution: The internal bisector of \(\angle AOB\) lies along the sum of the unit vectors of \(\overline{a}\) and \(\overline{b}\):\n\[\overline{v} = \frac{\overline{a}}{|\overline{a}|} + \frac{\overline{b}}{|\overline{b}|}.\]\nComparing with the given form \(\overline{v} = x\,\dfrac{\overline{a}}{|\overline{a}|} + y\,\dfrac{\overline{b}}{|\overline{b}|}\) gives \(x = 1\) and \(y = 1\), so \(x - y = 0\).

105.subtopic: Vector Geometry — Section Formula, Triangle, and Parallelogram
105.solution:
Place \(A = (0,0),\; B = (1,0),\; C = (0,1)\).

\(P\) divides \(BC\) in \(3:4\): \(P = \left(\dfrac{3\cdot 0 + 4\cdot 1}{7}, \dfrac{3\cdot 1 + 4\cdot 0}{7}ight) = \left(\dfrac{4}{7}, \dfrac{3}{7}ight)\).

\(Q\) divides \(CA\) in \(5:3\): \(Q = \left(\dfrac{5\cdot 0 + 3\cdot 0}{8}, \dfrac{5\cdot 0 + 3\cdot 1}{8}ight) = \left(0, \dfrac{3}{8}ight)\).

Point on \(AP\): \((x,y) = t\left(	frac{4}{7}, 	frac{3}{7}ight)\). Point on \(BQ\): \((1-s, 	frac{3s}{8})\). Equating: \(	frac{4t}{7} = 1 - s\) and \(	frac{3t}{7} = 	frac{3s}{8}\Rightarrow s = 	frac{8t}{7}\). Substituting, \(	frac{4t}{7} = 1 - 	frac{8t}{7}\Rightarrow 	frac{12t}{7} = 1 \Rightarrow t = 	frac{7}{12}\).

Thus \(AG:GP = t : (1-t) = 	frac{7}{12} : 	frac{5}{12} = 7:5\).

107.solution: For \(X \sim B(n,p)\), \(P(X=k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k q^{n-k}\).\n\[\frac{P(X=k)}{P(X=k-1)} = \frac{\binom{n}{k} p^k q^{n-k}}{\binom{n}{k-1} p^{k-1} q^{n-k+1}} = \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{\binom{n}{k-1}}\cdot \frac{p}{q}.\]\nSince \(\dfrac{\binom{n}{k}}{\binom{n}{k-1}} = \dfrac{n-k+1}{k}\), the ratio is \(\dfrac{n-k+1}{k}\cdot \dfrac{p}{q}\).

108.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions
108.solution: The family of lines through \((1,-1)\) is \(y + 1 = m(x-1)\), with one arbitrary constant \(m\). Differentiating: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = m\). Substituting back, \(y + 1 = \dfrac{dy}{dx}(x-1)\), i.e. \(y = (x-1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 1\).

109.solution:
Let \(y = \cos^{-1}\!\left(\sin\sqrt{	frac{1+x}{2}}ight) + x^x\) and \(u = \sqrt{	frac{1+x}{2}}\).

For the first part, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\cos^{-1}(\sin u) = \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{1-\sin^2 u}}\cdot \cos u\cdot u'\). With \(u = \sqrt{	frac{1+x}{2}}\), \(u' = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{	frac{1+x}{2}}}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot \dfrac{1}{u}\). At \(x=1\), \(u = 1\), \(\sqrt{1-\sin^2 1} = \cos 1\) and \(\cos u = \cos 1\), so that factor contributes \(\dfrac{-1}{\cos 1}\cdot \cos 1\cdot \dfrac{1}{4} = -\dfrac{1}{4}\).

For the second part, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}x^x = x^x(1+\ln x)\); at \(x=1\) this is \(1\cdot(1+0) = 1\).

Hence \(y'(1) = -\dfrac{1}{4} + 1 = \dfrac{3}{4}\).

110.solution: Equal projections of \(\overline{v}\) and \(\overline{w}\) along \(\overline{u}\) give \(\dfrac{\overline{v}\cdot\overline{u}}{|\overline{u}|} = \dfrac{\overline{w}\cdot\overline{u}}{|\overline{u}|}\), so \(\overline{u}\cdot\overline{v} = \overline{u}\cdot\overline{w}\). Also \(\overline{v}\perp\overline{w}\Rightarrow \overline{v}\cdot\overline{w} = 0\).\n\[|\overline{u}-\overline{v}+\overline{w}|^2 = |\overline{u}|^2 + |\overline{v}|^2 + |\overline{w}|^2 - 2\,\overline{u}\cdot\overline{v} + 2\,\overline{u}\cdot\overline{w} - 2\,\overline{v}\cdot\overline{w}.\]\nThe last three dot-product terms cancel/vanish, leaving \(1 + 4 + 9 = 14\). Hence the magnitude is \(\sqrt{14}\).

111.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines
111.solution: The parabola \(y^2 = 4x\) and \(y = |x|\) meet for \(x\ge 0\) where \(y = x\): \(x^2 = 4x \Rightarrow x = 0\) or \(x = 4\). On \([0,4]\) the parabola \(y = 2\sqrt{x}\) lies above \(y = x\).\n\[\text{Area} = \int_0^4 \left(2\sqrt{x} - x\right)dx = \left[\frac{4}{3}x^{3/2} - \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4 = \frac{4}{3}\cdot 8 - 8 = \frac{32}{3} - 8 = \frac{8}{3}\text{ sq. units}.\]\nBy symmetry the region for \(x\ge0\) (with \(y=|x|=x\)) gives this; the answer is \(\dfrac{8}{3}\) sq. units.

112.solution:
With \(	an A = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x(x^2+x+1)}}\) and \(	an B = \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}}\),
\[	an(A+B) =  rac{	an A + 	an B}{1 - 	an A	an B}.\]
Computing the numerator and denominator and simplifying gives \(	an(A+B) = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}}{x\sqrt{x}}\).

Also \(	an C = \sqrt{x^{-1}+x^{-2}+x^{-3}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{x^3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}}{x\sqrt{x}}\).

Since \(	an(A+B) = 	an C\), we get \(A + B = C\).

113.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance
113.solution:
Total probability: \(	frac{1}{5} + A + B = 1 \Rightarrow A + B = 	frac{4}{5}\).

\(E(X) = 30\cdot	frac{1}{5} + 10A + (-10)B = 4 \Rightarrow 6 + 10(A-B) = 4 \Rightarrow A - B = -	frac{1}{5}\).

Solving: \(A = 	frac{3}{10},\; B = 	frac{1}{2}\). Hence \(AB = 	frac{3}{10}\cdot	frac{1}{2} = 	frac{3}{20}\).

115.solution: Differentiate \(x^{2/5} + y^{2/5} = a^{2/5}\) implicitly:\n\[\frac{2}{5}x^{-3/5} + \frac{2}{5}y^{-3/5}\frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x^{-3/5}}{y^{-3/5}} = -\frac{y^{3/5}}{x^{3/5}} = -\sqrt[5]{\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3}.\]\nThe magnitude matches \(\sqrt[5]{(y/x)^3}\). Option D is the intended (printed without the sign) answer.
115.note: Strictly the derivative is negative, \(-\sqrt[5]{(y/x)^3}\); the printed options A and D both show \(\sqrt[5]{(y/x)^3}\) (option D with a trailing dot). Keyed D as the intended answer per the official key — a printed-paper defect (sign dropped from the option).

116.subtopic: Angle, Distance, and Geometry of Pair
116.solution: Factor: \((x-2y+1)^2 + k(x-2y+1) = (x-2y+1)(x-2y+1+k) = 0\), giving the parallel lines \(x-2y+1 = 0\) and \(x-2y+(1+k) = 0\).\n\nPerpendicular distance \(= \dfrac{|1 - (1+k)|}{\sqrt{1^2+(-2)^2}} = \dfrac{|k|}{\sqrt{5}}\). Setting \(\dfrac{|k|}{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{5}\) gives \(|k| = 5\), so \(k = 5\).

118.solution:
Since \(\angle A = 90^\circ\), \(B + C = 90^\circ\), so \(	frac{B}{2} + 	frac{C}{2} = 45^\circ\).

Roots: \(	an	frac{B}{2} + 	an	frac{C}{2} = -	frac{b}{a}\), \(	an	frac{B}{2}	an	frac{C}{2} = 	frac{c}{a}\).

\(	an\!\left(	frac{B}{2}+	frac{C}{2}ight) = 	an 45^\circ = 1 = \dfrac{-b/a}{1 - c/a} = \dfrac{-b}{a-c}\). Thus \(a - c = -b\), i.e. \(a + b = c\).

119.solution: Take the symmetric case \(a = b = c = 1\): then \(r^2 = 3\), \(r = \sqrt3\), and each argument equals \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\), so each term is \(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\).\n\nSum \(= 3\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) (the identity holds in general).

The plane contains \(A(2,1,2)\) and \(B(1,2,1)\), so \(\overrightarrow{AB} = (-1,1,-1)\). It is parallel to the line \(2x = 3y,\; z = 1\), i.e. \(	frac{x}{3} = 	frac{y}{2},\; z = 1\), direction \(\overrightarrow{d} = (3,2,0)\).

Normal \(\overrightarrow{n} = \overrightarrow{AB}	imes\overrightarrow{d} = (1\cdot0 - (-1)\cdot2,\; (-1)\cdot3 - (-1)\cdot0,\; (-1)\cdot2 - 1\cdot3) = (2, -3, -5)\).

123.solution: Tossing 3 coins, \(P(\text{all heads or all tails}) = \tfrac{2}{8} = \tfrac14\) (win ₹150) and \(P(\text{one or two heads}) = \tfrac{6}{8} = \tfrac34\) (lose ₹50).\n\n\(E = \tfrac14(150) + \tfrac34(-50) = 37.5 - 37.5 = 0\). He neither wins nor loses on average.

125.solution:
By the cosine rule with \(a = \sqrt3 - 2,\; b = \sqrt3 + 2,\; C = 60^\circ\):
\[c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos 60^\circ.\]
\(a^2 = 7 - 4\sqrt3,\; b^2 = 7 + 4\sqrt3\Rightarrow a^2 + b^2 = 14\). \(ab = (\sqrt3)^2 - 2^2 = -1\), so \(-2ab\cos60^\circ = -2(-1)(	frac12) = 1\).

Thus \(c^2 = 14 + 1 = 15\), \(c = \sqrt{15}\) units.

127.solution: \(|A| = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 4 + 2 = 6\), so \(A^{-1} = \tfrac16\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).\n\nWith \(A^{-1} = \alpha I + \beta A\), comparing the \((1,1)\) entry: \(\alpha + \beta = \tfrac{4}{6} = \tfrac{2}{3}\) (the \((2,2)\) entry gives \(\alpha + 4\beta = \tfrac16\), consistent). Hence \(4(\alpha + \beta) = 4\cdot\tfrac23 = \tfrac83\).

128.subtopic: Negation, Equivalence, Tautology, and Switch Circuits
128.solution: Reading the circuits: (A) two parallel branches \(S_1\)-\(S_2\) (series) and \(S_1\)-\(S_3\) (series) gives \((p\land q)\lor(p\land r)\). (B) \(S_1\) in parallel with the series \(S_2\)-\(S_3\) gives \(p\lor(q\land r)\). (C) \(S_1\) in series with parallel \(S_2\),\(S_3\) gives \(p\land(q\lor r)\). (D) \(S_1\),\(S_2\),\(S_3\) all in series gives \(p\land q\land r\). (E) series \(S_1\)-\(S_2\) in parallel with \(S_3\) gives \((p\land q)\lor r\).\n\nBy the distributive law, \((p\land q)\lor(p\land r) = p\land(q\lor r)\), so circuits (A) and (C) are equivalent.
128.note: AK answer is D = '(C) and (E)', but C = p∧(q∨r) and E = (p∧q)∨r are NOT equivalent (e.g. p=F,q=F,r=T: C=F, E=T). The equivalent pair is (A) and (C): (p∧q)∨(p∧r) = p∧(q∨r) by distributivity — which is also what the AK's OWN solution concludes ('(A) and (C) are equivalent'). The correct option is the one reading '(A) and (C)'; option B's extracted text is the garbled '(A) and (C)'. Keyed B and fixed its option text via optionOverrides.

129.solution: Put \(v = x + y\), so \(\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1\). The equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x+y)^2\) becomes \(\dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1 = v^2\Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{v^2+1} = dx\).\n\nIntegrating: \(\tan^{-1}v = x + c\), i.e. \(\tan^{-1}(x+y) = x + c\).

130.solution:
The plane through the intersection line is \((x+y+z-1) + \lambda(3x+4y+5z-2) = 0\), i.e. \((1+3\lambda)x + (1+4\lambda)y + (1+5\lambda)z - (1+2\lambda) = 0\).

Perpendicular to the XY-plane \(\Rightarrow\) coefficient of \(z\) is \(0\): \(1 + 5\lambda = 0\Rightarrow \lambda = -	frac15\).

Substituting: \(	frac25 x + 	frac15 y - 	frac35 = 0\Rightarrow 2x + y - 3 = 0\).

131.solution: The normal at \(P(x,y)\) has slope \(-\tfrac{1}{y'}\) and meets the X-axis at \(Q = \left(x + y\,\tfrac{dy}{dx},\,0\right)\). Then\n\[l(PQ)^2 = \left(y\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + y^2 = k^2 \Rightarrow y\frac{dy}{dx} = \pm\sqrt{k^2 - y^2}.\]\nSeparating, \(\dfrac{y\,dy}{\sqrt{k^2-y^2}} = \pm dx\), integrating: \(-\sqrt{k^2-y^2} = \pm x + c\). Through \((0,k)\), \(c = 0\), so \(k^2 - y^2 = x^2\), i.e. \(x^2 + y^2 = k^2\).

132.subtopic: Continuity at a Point — Finding Parameters
132.solution:
For continuity, \(f(0) = \displaystyle\lim_{x	o0} rac{(27-2x)^{1/3} - 3}{9 - 3(243+5x)^{1/5}}\) (a \(	frac00\) form).

By L'Hopital's rule:
\[f(0) = \lim_{x	o0} rac{	frac13(27-2x)^{-2/3}(-2)}{-	frac35(243+5x)^{-4/5}(5)}.\]
At \(x=0\): numerator \(= 	frac13\cdot 9^{-1}\cdot(-2) = -	frac{2}{27}\); denominator \(= -3\cdot 3^{-4} = -	frac{3}{81} = -	frac{1}{27}\). Ratio \(= \dfrac{-2/27}{-1/27} = 2\).

133.solution:
For \(x < 0\): \(\dfrac{|x|}{|x|+x^2} = \dfrac{-x}{-x+x^2} = \dfrac{-1}{-1+x}	o 1\) as \(x	o0^-\).

For \(x > 0\): \(\dfrac{x}{x+x^2} = \dfrac{1}{1+x}	o 1\) as \(x	o0^+\).

Both one-sided limits equal \(1\), so the limit is \(1\).

134.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
134.solution: \(f(x) = \sin^7 x\cos^{16}x\). Then \(f(-x) = (-\sin x)^7(\cos x)^{16} = -\sin^7 x\cos^{16}x = -f(x)\), an odd function. The integral of an odd function over the symmetric interval \([-3,3]\) is \(0\).

135.subtopic: Distance, Foot of Perpendicular, Projection, and Mirror Image
135.solution:
The foot \(Q\) lies on the line through \(P(-1,1,2)\) along the plane's normal \((2,-3,1)\): \(x = -1+2t,\; y = 1-3t,\; z = 2+t\).

Substitute into \(2x - 3y + z - 11 = 0\): \(2(-1+2t) - 3(1-3t) + (2+t) - 11 = 0\Rightarrow 14t - 14 = 0\Rightarrow t = 1\).

So \(Q = (1, -2, 3)\).

136.solution: For \(^{7-x}P_{x-1}\) to be defined: the lower index \(r = x-1\) must be a whole number \(\ge 0\Rightarrow x \ge 1\); the upper index \(n = 7-x\) must be a natural number; and \(r \le n\): \(x-1 \le 7-x\Rightarrow 2x \le 8\Rightarrow x \le 4\).\n\nWith \(x\) a positive integer, \(x \in \{1,2,3,4\}\).

137.subtopic: Trigonometric Integrals - Rational and Substitution Forms
137.solution: \(\displaystyle\int\frac{x+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\,dx = \int\frac{x}{2\cos^2(x/2)}\,dx + \int\frac{2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)}{2\cos^2(x/2)}\,dx = \frac12\int x\sec^2\tfrac{x}{2}\,dx + \int\tan\tfrac{x}{2}\,dx\).\n\nIntegrating the first by parts: \(\tfrac12\left[x\cdot 2\tan\tfrac{x}{2} - \int 2\tan\tfrac{x}{2}\,dx\right] = x\tan\tfrac{x}{2} - \int\tan\tfrac{x}{2}\,dx\). This cancels the remaining \(\int\tan\tfrac{x}{2}\,dx\), leaving \(x\tan\tfrac{x}{2} + c\).

138.solution:
\(|\overline{a}-\overline{b}|^2 + |\overline{b}-\overline{c}|^2 + |\overline{c}-\overline{a}|^2 = 2(|\overline{a}|^2+|\overline{b}|^2+|\overline{c}|^2) - 2(\overline{a}\cdot\overline{b}+\overline{b}\cdot\overline{c}+\overline{c}\cdot\overline{a})\).

With \(|\overline{a}|^2+|\overline{b}|^2+|\overline{c}|^2 = 9+25+49 = 83\), this is \(166 - 2S\) where \(S = \overline{a}\cdot\overline{b}+\overline{b}\cdot\overline{c}+\overline{c}\cdot\overline{a}\).

Since \(|\overline{a}+\overline{b}+\overline{c}|^2 \ge 0\Rightarrow 83 + 2S \ge 0\Rightarrow -2S \le 83\). Hence the expression \(\le 166 + 83 = 249\).

139.solution:
\(\gcd(n,36) = 2\) means \(n\) is divisible by \(2\) but not by \(4\) and not by \(3\) (since \(36 = 2^2\cdot3^2\)).

Three-digit multiples of \(2\): \(\dfrac{998-100}{2}+1 = 450\).
Minus those divisible by \(3\) too, i.e. by \(6\): \(\dfrac{996-102}{6}+1 = 150\).
Minus those divisible by \(4\): \(\dfrac{996-100}{4}+1 = 225\).
Add back those divisible by \(12\) (counted twice): \(\dfrac{996-108}{12}+1 = 75\).

By inclusion-exclusion: \(450 - (150 + 225 - 75) = 450 - 300 = 150\).

140.subtopic: Algebraic Equations, Locus, and Cube Roots
140.solution:
Let \(z = x+iy\). For \(\dfrac{z-1}{2z+1}\) to be purely imaginary, its real part is \(0\). Rationalising, the real part numerator is \((x-1)(2x+1) + 2y^2 = 2x^2 + 2y^2 - x - 1\).

Setting it to \(0\): \(2x^2 + 2y^2 - x - 1 = 0\Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 - 	frac{x}{2} = 	frac12\Rightarrow \left(x-	frac14ight)^2 + y^2 = 	frac{9}{16}\).

Radius \(= \sqrt{	frac{9}{16}} = 	frac34\) units.

141.solution:
\(\int	an^4 x\,dx = \int(\sec^2 x - 1)^2\,dx = \int(\sec^4 x - 2\sec^2 x + 1)\,dx\).

\(\int\sec^4 x\,dx = \int(1+	an^2 x)\sec^2 x\,dx = 	an x + 	frac{	an^3 x}{3}\). So
\[\int	an^4 x\,dx = 	an x + 	frac{	an^3 x}{3} - 2	an x + x = 	frac13	an^3 x - 	an x + x + k.\]
Thus \(a = 	frac13,\; b = -1,\; c = 1\), and \(a - b + c = 	frac13 + 1 + 1 = 	frac73\).

142.solution: For coplanarity of the two lines, \(\begin{vmatrix} x_2-x_1 & y_2-y_1 & z_2-z_1 \\ a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \end{vmatrix} = 0\) with \((x_2-x_1,\ldots) = (1,1,-2)\), \((a_1,b_1,c_1) = (1,1,-k)\), \((a_2,b_2,c_2) = (k,1,2)\).\n\[\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & -k \\ k & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 1(2+k) - 1(2+k^2) - 2(1-k) = 0.\]\nThis gives \(k^2 - 3k + 2 = 0\Rightarrow (k-1)(k-2) = 0\Rightarrow k = 1\) or \(2\).

143.solution: Partial fractions: \(\dfrac{x}{(x-1)(x-2)} = \dfrac{-1}{x-1} + \dfrac{2}{x-2}\) (since at \(x=1\) residue \(=\tfrac{1}{-1}=-1\), at \(x=2\) residue \(=\tfrac{2}{1}=2\)).\n\[\int = -\ln|x-1| + 2\ln|x-2| + c = \ln\left|\frac{(x-2)^2}{x-1}\right| + c.\]

144.subtopic: Basic Probability — Events, Conditional, and Complement
144.solution: With \(A,B\) independent: \(P(A\cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A)P(B)\). So \(\tfrac{11}{20} = P(A) + \tfrac25 - \tfrac25 P(A)\Rightarrow \tfrac{3}{20} = \tfrac35 P(A)\Rightarrow P(A) = \tfrac14\), hence \(P(A') = \tfrac34\).\n\nSince \(A'\) and \(B\) are independent, \(P(A'\mid B) = P(A') = \tfrac34\). Now \(x = \tfrac34\) is a root of \(4x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0\) (which factors as \((4x-3)(x-1) = 0\)).

145.subtopic: Tangent, Normal, Approximation, and Curve from Geometric Condition
145.solution:
Differentiate \(y = \cos(x+y)\): \(y' = -\sin(x+y)(1+y')\Rightarrow y'(1+\sin(x+y)) = -\sin(x+y)\Rightarrow y' = \dfrac{-\sin(x+y)}{1+\sin(x+y)}\).

Parallel to \(x+2y=0\) (slope \(-	frac12\)): \(\dfrac{-\sin(x+y)}{1+\sin(x+y)} = -	frac12\Rightarrow 1+\sin(x+y) = 2\sin(x+y)\Rightarrow \sin(x+y) = 1\Rightarrow x+y = 	frac{\pi}{2}\).

Then \(y = \cos(x+y) = \cos	frac{\pi}{2} = 0\), so the point is \(\left(	frac{\pi}{2},0ight)\). Tangent: \(y - 0 = -	frac12\left(x - 	frac{\pi}{2}ight)\Rightarrow 2x + 4y - \pi = 0\).

146.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection
146.solution: \(9x^2 + 5y^2 - 30y = 0\Rightarrow 9x^2 + 5(y-3)^2 = 45\Rightarrow \dfrac{x^2}{5} + \dfrac{(y-3)^2}{9} = 1\).\n\nHere the major axis is along \(y\) with \(b^2 = 9 > a^2 = 5\). Eccentricity \(e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{a^2}{b^2}} = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac59} = \sqrt{\tfrac49} = \tfrac23\).

147.solution:
Curve \(x^2 = y - 6\): \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x\), at \((1,7)\) slope \(= 2\). Tangent: \(y - 7 = 2(x-1)\Rightarrow 2x - y + 5 = 0\).

Circle \(x^2+y^2+16x+12y+C=0\) has centre \((-8,-6)\), radius \(\sqrt{64+36-C} = \sqrt{100-C}\). Tangency: distance from centre to line equals radius:
\[\left| rac{2(-8) - (-6) + 5}{\sqrt{4+1}}ight| = \sqrt{100-C}\Rightarrow \left| rac{-5}{\sqrt5}ight| = \sqrt5 = \sqrt{100-C}\Rightarrow 5 = 100 - C\Rightarrow C = 95.\]

148.subtopic: Roots — Nature, Vieta's Relations, and Conditions
148.solution:
For \(x^2 - (a-2)x - a + 1 = 0\): \(\alpha +  eta = a - 2\), \(\alpha eta = 1 - a\).

\(\alpha^2 +  eta^2 = (\alpha+ eta)^2 - 2\alpha eta = (a-2)^2 - 2(1-a) = a^2 - 2a + 2\).

This quadratic in \(a\) is minimum at \(a = -\dfrac{-2}{2(1)} = 1\).

150.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection
150.solution:
For \(x^2 - 4y^2 = 2\): \(2x - 8y y' = 0\Rightarrow m_1 = \dfrac{x}{4y}\). For \(8x^2 = 40 - my^2\): \(16x = -2my y'\Rightarrow m_2 = \dfrac{-8x}{my}\).

Orthogonality \(m_1 m_2 = -1\): \(\dfrac{x}{4y}\cdot\dfrac{-8x}{my} = -1\Rightarrow \dfrac{2x^2}{my^2} = 1\Rightarrow x^2 = \dfrac{my^2}{2}\).

Substituting into the first curve: \(\dfrac{my^2}{2} - 4y^2 = 2\Rightarrow y^2 = \dfrac{4}{m-8}\). Into the second: \(8\cdot\dfrac{my^2}{2} = 40 - my^2\Rightarrow y^2 = \dfrac{8}{m}\). Equating: \(\dfrac{4}{m-8} = \dfrac{8}{m}\Rightarrow 4m = 8m - 64\Rightarrow m = 16\).
